Comment: Shared cutover: ONE state machine for every DMS task. Start with {"taskArn": "..."}. Stop DMS -> drain CDC -> stop this task's CDC run -> drop _cdc_file -> delete this task's Glue jobs. The task's folder and job names are found by its ARN, so renaming the DMS task does not break cutover.

CheckInput.Comment: Start input must be {"taskArn": "..."}; everything else comes from config/pipeline.json and the DMS task.

MissingTaskArn.Cause: Start this workflow with input {"taskArn": "arn:aws:dms:<region>:<account>:task:<id>"}. Optional: "taskSuffix" (override the folder/job name), "adoptExistingFolder": true (startup only).

CutoverResolveTask.Comment: Settings + this task's folder, CDC job name and cdc_root (resolve_task shared mode, read-only).

StartupOverrideGate.Comment: If this task's STARTUP was finished with override=true (the startup-override marker is present -> $.resolved.startupOverrideUsed), its data was accepted past a validation failure. Refuse the cutover UNLESS it, too, was started with override=true, so unvalidated data can never be cut over silently. Both reads are IsPresent-guarded (older resolve_task that returns neither -> behaves as no startup override, so cutover proceeds as before). Otherwise continue to the normal pre-DMS-stop validation gate.

StartupOverrideRequiresOverride.Cause: This task's startup was completed WITH override=true (its data was accepted past a validation failure; see config/_task/<suffix>/_overrides/). Cutting it over would move unvalidated data, so this cutover refuses. If you have reviewed the overridden validation result and accept it, start a NEW cutover execution with input {"taskArn": "...", "override": true} (optional "overrideReason") to accept it. Nothing was touched: DMS is still running and CDC is still running.

CdcValidationPreCheck.Comment: BEFORE stopping DMS: fail fast if any UNRESOLVED cdc_control.cdc_validation_failures rows exist for this task's tables. Reuses drain-check in mode=validation_gate (it already reads DSQL + the manifest index). Nothing is touched here, so on failure DMS is still running and CDC is still running. A task with no failures table / no tables counts as 0 and passes.

CdcValidationPreGate.Comment: Pass only when there are zero unresolved validation failures. Otherwise stop the cutover before touching DMS — UNLESS the cutover was started with override=true, in which case the failures are logged (LogPreValidationOverride) and the cutover continues. The override comparison is IsPresent-guarded for the audit.

LogPreValidationOverride.Comment: override=true: unresolved CDC-validation failures existed at the pre-DMS-stop check but are being bypassed on the operator's explicit instruction. Record what was bypassed on the execution (nothing has been touched yet; the drain/stop/delete safety ordering below is unchanged) and continue.

DescribeBeforeStop.Comment: M02 re-runnability: describe the DMS task BEFORE trying to stop it. If a previous cutover already stopped it (any reason), stopReplicationTask would raise InvalidResourceStateFault and (pre-fix) fail the whole re-run. Instead, skip the stop when the task is already 'stopped' and continue straight to the stop-confirm loop. Only an actually-running/starting task is stopped.

IsAlreadyStopped.Comment: Already 'stopped' (incl. STOPPED_AFTER_CACHED_EVENTS / any stop reason, which DMS reports as status 'stopped') -> skip StopCdcDmsTask and go straight to the stop-confirm loop (idempotent re-run). Anything else (running/starting) -> stop it.

CdcValidationFailedPre.Comment: Build a Cause naming each table and its unresolved-failure count, then fail. DMS is still running and CDC is still running — nothing was touched.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('CDC validation found unresolved failures BEFORE DMS was stopped (DMS still running, CDC still running). Investigate cdc_control.cdc_validation_failures and clear with UPDATE ... SET resolved=true after review. Total={}, byTable={}', $.validationPre.failures, States.JsonToString($.validationPre.byTable))

ResolveFailed.Comment: Shows the resolve-task error (bad settings, DMS task check, folder owner check).

Catch.Comment: M02: the task was already stopped (or not in a stoppable state) between DescribeBeforeStop and here. Treat as already stopped and continue to the confirm loop; do not fail the re-run.

WaitValidationSettle.Comment: The drain confirmed every applied file is 'done', but each file's Tier-2 validation runs AFTER its commit (re-read + a VALIDATION_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS=5s recheck). Wait comfortably longer than that recheck window (plus margin) so any in-flight validation of the LAST applied files has finished and recorded before the final gate reads the table. DMS is already stopped, so no new files arrive during this wait.

CdcValidationFinalCheck.Comment: AFTER the drain completed and BEFORE StopCdcRun / DropTags / DeleteGlueJobs: re-count unresolved cdc_control.cdc_validation_failures for this task's tables. DMS is already stopped at this point, but the CDC run, _cdc_file column and Glue jobs are all still untouched, so a failure here leaves everything downstream in place for investigation.

CdcValidationFinalGate.Comment: Pass only with zero unresolved validation failures. Otherwise stop before StopCdcRun (CDC run + jobs stay) — UNLESS the cutover was started with override=true, in which case the failures are logged (LogFinalValidationOverride) and the cutover continues to StopCdcRun. The safety ordering (DMS already stopped; drain already complete) is unchanged; only the refuse-gate is bypassed.

LogFinalValidationOverride.Comment: override=true: unresolved CDC-validation failures remain after the drain but are being bypassed on the operator's explicit instruction. DMS is already stopped and the drain is complete; the CDC run, _cdc_file column and Glue jobs are still untouched. Record what was bypassed and continue to StopCdcRun (the safety ordering is unchanged).

CdcValidationFailedFinal.Comment: Unresolved validation failures after the drain. DMS is stopped; the CDC run, _cdc_file column and Glue jobs are all still untouched. Build a Cause naming each table and count, then fail.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('CDC validation found unresolved failures AFTER the drain completed (DMS stopped; CDC run, _cdc_file and Glue jobs untouched). Investigate cdc_control.cdc_validation_failures and clear with UPDATE ... SET resolved=true after review, then re-run cutover. Total={}, byTable={}', $.validationFinal.failures, States.JsonToString($.validationFinal.byTable))

CdcValidationFailed.Comment: CDC validation (Tier-2 by-key net-state check) recorded unresolved discrepancies in cdc_control.cdc_validation_failures. Cutover MUST stop until an operator reviews each row and clears it with UPDATE cdc_control.cdc_validation_failures SET resolved=true WHERE table_name='...' (never DELETE). The exact tables + counts are in the Cause.

StopCdcRun.Comment: B27: a 2nd cutover of an already-cut-over task reaches here after the 1st cutover deleted the CDC job. The stop-cdc-run Lambda now treats a missing job as alreadyStopped (jobMissing=true); this Retry/Catch is defense-in-depth so even an un-redeployed Lambda that still raises Glue.EntityNotFoundException is treated as a no-op (job already gone -> nothing to stop) and cutover continues instead of failing. Real errors (AccessDenied, throttling) are NOT EntityNotFound, so they still retry and then fail closed at CutoverFailed.

Catch.Comment: The CDC job no longer exists (a prior cutover deleted it); nothing to stop. Skip to the fork stop/delete steps, which also tolerate already-gone jobs.

ListForkCdcJobs.Comment: Find THIS task's fork CDC jobs (ck-* and bg-*) by EXACT TAG (project+task) UNION the per-task registry _jobs.json — never by name prefix — so every fork's CDC run can be stopped before the jobs are deleted, and stale ones are caught. Returns [] when the task has no forks.

StopForkCdcRuns.Comment: Stop EACH composite fork's CDC run for this task (same stop-cdc-run Lambda, each fork's own job name + the task's config prefix). Empty list -> no iterations. A fork job already gone is tolerated (EntityNotFound skipped); DeleteGlueJobs removes it by prefix anyway.

Catch.Comment: This fork CDC job no longer exists; nothing to stop. DeleteGlueJobs removes it by prefix. Do not fail cutover.

InitDeleteLoop.Comment: B21: cutover retries DeleteGlueJobs in a loop (Wait -> delete) until nothing is pending or the budget runs out. c counts the passes; at 10s + ~30s delete per pass, 120 passes is a generous ~60-80 min ceiling for a composite CDC run that is slow to stop.

DeleteGlueJobs.Comment: B20: the delete Lambda needs the account id to build job ARNs for the get_tags lookup; pass account_id ($.resolved.accountId) AND dms_task_arn ($.taskArn, which the cutover input always carries) so it never fails to resolve the account (the Lambda also falls back to its own context ARN / STS). Deletes this task's Glue jobs; a job whose CDC run is still stopping is returned under 'pending' (B21) and retried by the loop below, not left orphaned.

AllGlueJobsDeleted.Comment: Order matters: a hard 'failed' (couldn't delete for a non-pending reason) ends at GlueJobsNotDeletedList; a 'pending' job (its CDC run is still stopping, B21) loops back after a short wait until the budget runs out; otherwise every job is gone -> success. 'failed'/'pending' lists are absent on older Lambda versions (treated as none).

CutoverOverrideTerminal.Comment: Every Glue job is deleted — the task is cut over. If this cutover was started with override=true (it bypassed a validation gate and/or accepted a startup override), write the cutover override record and end in the distinct CutoverSucceededWithOverride; otherwise end in the normal CutoverSucceeded. The read is IsPresent-guarded so an older resolve_task (no $.resolved.override) ends in CutoverSucceeded exactly as before.

WriteCutoverOverrideRecord.Comment: Write the cutover override audit record to config/_task/<suffix>/_overrides/<execution>.json (who=execution ARN, when, reason, bypassed gates). workflow=cutover, so NO startup-override marker is written. Reuses resolve_task (mode write_override_record).

Catch.Comment: The cutover itself is complete (DMS stopped, drained, CDC stopped, jobs deleted); only writing the audit record failed. Record the error but still end in CutoverSucceededWithOverride — the migration is cut over and must not be reported as failed.

CutoverSucceededWithOverride.Comment: Cutover finished WITH override: a validation gate was bypassed and/or a startup override was accepted on the operator's explicit instruction. The safety ordering (DMS stop -> drain -> stop CDC runs -> delete jobs) was NOT bypassed. $.overrideRecord has the audit record key, who/when and the bypassed gates.

DeleteBudgetLeft.Comment: B21: keep looping DeleteGlueJobs while jobs are still pending, up to the budget. Past the budget, end in GlueJobsNotDeleted naming the still-pending jobs so an operator can finish by hand.

WaitDeleteRetry.Comment: Give the slow (composite) CDC run time to actually stop before the next delete pass. The delete Lambda already force batch-stopped it; this just lets the run reach a stopped state.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('Cutover stopped DMS, drained CDC and dropped _cdc_file, but these Glue jobs still had a CDC run that would not stop within the delete budget, so they were not deleted: {}. Stop their runs and delete them by hand (aws glue batch-stop-job-run / aws glue delete-job --job-name <name>), or re-run cutover.', States.JsonToString($.deleteJobs.Payload.pending))

GlueJobsNotDeleted.Comment: The migration itself is cut over: DMS is stopped, every CDC file was applied, the CDC job is stopped and the _cdc_file column is dropped. Only deleting the task's Glue jobs failed; the cause names them. Delete them by hand (aws glue delete-job --job-name <name>), or start the cutover again.

CutoverFailed.Cause: A cutover step failed. See execution history.

CdcDrainTimedOut.Cause: CDC did not catch up to the latest S3 CSV within the drain budget. Investigate, then re-run cutover.
